course_name_original: Elementos de Máquinas y Sistemas Mecatrónicos

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the basic knowledge for the design of machine elements, allowing the student to discern the load states of one of these elements in a mechanical system, apply the calculation and selection criteria, and advantageously use computer calculation applications and databases.
Produce and interpret technical specifications that include the machine elements covered in the course, using technical language, and understanding the important design parameters in each case.

Students should be able to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving capacity in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, which includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students should possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.

Develop technical specifications that allow a problem in mechatronic engineering to be approached while maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural, or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Evaluate the viability of new mechatronic products, based on their technological characteristics, manufacturing possibilities, and other socio-economic factors related to their potential implementation.
Select the material, dimension, and optimize the shape of mechatronic system elements, considering resistance, durability, and reliability criteria.
Justify in a well-founded manner the different options for the automation of a mechatronic machine or technological process.

Students will be able to simulate and calculate, from both a kinematic and resistant point of view, a mechanism based on standard elements such as gears, articulated links, linear guides, cams, flexible transmissions, etc.
Students will be able to prepare a technical specification for mechanical elements, suitable for certain operating conditions, gears, bearings, brakes and clutches, couplings, etc.
Students will acquire skill in the use of ICT, to access databases and spreadsheets for various commercial machine elements. This will allow them to delve into a project to a detailed design.

syllabus_topics: Practical calculation of machine elements. Principles.
Fatigue in the design of machine elements.
Shafts and axles, accessories. Design and calculation.
Bearings and couplings. Types, selection. Catalogs.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to face-to-face classes and submission of proposed class exercises and practice scripts
Exam demonstrating knowledge for problem-solving and practical questions

assessment_rules: 25% of the grade will be based on attendance to face-to-face classes and submission of proposed class exercises and practice scripts. 75% of the grade will be obtained from an exam, in which students can use all class notes and demonstrate their knowledge to solve practical problems and questions.
